label: prf:categorical-mass-markov
title: Proof of categorical mass markov
html:
Proof

The chain has three steps.

Step 1 (Mass integrand = identity). By definition (mass), \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert \int_A \circ \Psi \circ \varrho \rVert with \Psi = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta. The unit law and the Frobenius relation give \Psi = L_u, left multiplication by u = \Psi \circ \eta. When the Frobenius form is the counit, \int_A = \varepsilon, the counit law (\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta = \mathrm{id}_A gives \Psi = \mathrm{id}_A, hence

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \Bigl\lVert \textstyle\int_A \varrho \Bigr\rVert .

The reason is the counit law. It is not the Nakayama automorphism or S^2 = \mathrm{id}: \Psi is a left multiplication, and it is the identity exactly when u = \eta.

Step 2 (Frobenius form = Markov trace = quantum trace of the multiplicative integral). Take \int_A to be the normalised Jones–Markov trace. It is realised on V^{\otimes n}, V = R^2, through Jimbo's R-matrix \check R. A braid word \ell_1 \cdots \ell_k has transports T(\sigma_a) = \check R_a and T(\sigma_a^{-1}) = \check R_a - (q - q^{-1}), acting at strands a, a+1. Its multiplicative integral is the ordered product \mathrm{Hol}(\beta) = T(\ell_1) \cdots T(\ell_k), and

  \textstyle\int_A \rho(\beta)
  \;=\; (1 + q^2)^{-n} \, \mathrm{Tr}\bigl( K^{\otimes n} \cdot \mathrm{Hol}(\beta) \bigr),
  \qquad K = \mathrm{diag}(1, q^2).

This functional is cyclic. It satisfies the positive and negative Markov moves with scalars q^3/(q^2+1) and q^{-1}/(q^2+1), and \int_A 1 = 1. The weight K is not chosen: the Markov move exists only for K = \mathrm{diag}(1, q^2) up to scale. This is Turaev's enhanced Yang–Baxter operator (\check R, K, \alpha = q^2, \beta = q).

The categorical trace of A acting on itself is not this functional. It is the regular trace, which fails the Markov property: on H_3(q) the normalised regular trace gives \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_1 \sigma_2) = h^2/6 against \mathrm{tr}(\sigma_1)^2 = h^2/4, with h = q - q^{-1}.

Step 3 (Mass = trace of cycle). Combining Steps 1 and 2:

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}
  \;=\; \Bigl\lVert \textstyle\int_A \bigl(
    \underbrace{(\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta}_{= \,\mathrm{id}_A}
    \circ\, \varrho \bigr) \Bigr\rVert
  \;=\; \Bigl|\!\int_A\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})\Bigr|
  \;=\; (1 + q^2)^{-n} \, \bigl| \mathrm{Tr}\bigl( K^{\otimes n} \cdot \mathrm{Hol}(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \bigr) \bigr| .

Scope. Steps 1 and 2 are proved over a generic commutative ring, building on the cyclicity, peel and normalisation properties of the Markov trace. The descent to braid classes is proved: on the tower of Artin braid groups the framing-corrected trace is invariant under conjugation and both stabilisations, every braid is spelled by a word, and the identity of Step 2 holds on braid classes. Three points are not proved here.

  1. Which algebra carries the Frobenius structure. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the Ocneanu weights vanish on every three-row shape. So the pairing (x, y) \mapsto \int_A xy is degenerate on H_n(q) for n \ge 3, and (H_n(q), \int_A) is not a Frobenius algebra. The Frobenius object is the quotient by the radical of this pairing, H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}. On it the form is non-degenerate for q > 1, because the surviving two-row weights y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^{\,n} are strictly positive. Positivity holds for the sesquilinear form (x, y) \mapsto \int_A x\,y^{*}, with * the conjugate-linear anti-involution fixing each \sigma_i; the bilinear form itself is indefinite. That this quotient is the Temperley–Lieb algebra \mathrm{TL}_n(q) is not proved here.
  2. That the Frobenius form is the counit. This is the hypothesis of Step 1. It holds when \Delta is the coproduct induced by \int_A, and has to be checked for the Frobenius–Hopf data actually used.
  3. The continuous holonomy. \mathrm{Hol} is a finite ordered product. That the holonomy of the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection along a braid equals such a product of R-matrices is the Drinfeld–Kohno theorem. For \mathfrak{sl}_2 the precise statement is Kohno's Theorems 1.2.8 and 2.2.4: the monodromy of \omega=\lambda\sum\Omega_{\alpha\beta}\,d\log(z_\alpha-z_\beta) sends \sigma_i to q^{\nu} times the Hecke generator, with q=e^{-\pi i\lambda}, and only up to conjugation by an analytic P(\lambda). The scalar q^{\nu} is a writhe factor. The conjugation leaves the plain trace unchanged. For the weighted trace, Kohno's particular P(\lambda) is not shown to preserve total weight, but a weight-preserving replacement exists, which is all the trace needs. Write H_{\mathrm{tot}} for the total weight, so that K^{\otimes n}=q^{n}q^{-H_{\mathrm{tot}}}. (i) \Omega is \mathfrak{g}-invariant, so the monodromy \theta commutes with the diagonal \mathfrak{g}-action and V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V_j\otimes M_j as \mathfrak{g}\times B_n-modules; on the R-matrix side V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V^{q}_j\otimes M^{q}_j by q-Schur–Weyl duality [jimbo1986], with the M^{q}_j irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic for q not a root of unity. (ii) The two B_n-images are conjugate, so their commutants have the same dimension, \sum_j(2j+1)^2. On the monodromy side the commutant contains the image of U(\mathfrak{g}), \bigoplus_j\mathrm{End}(V_j)\otimes 1, of exactly that dimension, so it equals it. By the double commutant theorem the M_j are irreducible and pairwise non-isomorphic, each occurring 2j+1 times. (iii) Since P(\lambda) is a B_n-isomorphism, irreducibles with equal multiplicity correspond, and the multiplicities 2j+1 are distinct, so M_j\cong M^{q}_j via some \varphi_j. Choosing weight-preserving linear isomorphisms \psi_j:V_j\to V^{q}_j (each weight space is one-dimensional), P'=\bigoplus_j\psi_j\otimes\varphi_j intertwines the two B_n-actions and commutes with H_{\mathrm{tot}}. Hence, for generic \lambda, \mathrm{Tr}\big(K^{\otimes n}\mathrm{Hol}(\beta)\big)=q^{-\nu\,w(\beta)}\,\mathrm{Tr}\big(q^{n}q^{-H_{\mathrm{tot}}}\,\theta(\beta)\big)=q^{-\nu\,w(\beta)}\sum_j \mathrm{Tr}_{V_j}\big(q^{n}q^{-H}\big)\,\chi_{M_j}\big(\theta(\beta)\big), with w(\beta) the writhe. Check at n=2: \mathrm{Tr}(K\otimes K\,\check R)=q+q^{2}(q-q^{-1})+q^{5}=q^{3}+q^{5}, which equals the triplet-plus-singlet sum q(1+q^{2}+q^{4})-q^{-1}q^{2}. Two conventions are not fixed here: the orientation q\leftrightarrow q^{-1} between e^{-\pi i\lambda} and the Jimbo parameter, and the normalisation of \Omega, which moves the per-crossing scalar. Neither changes the argument. It needs q not a root of unity and says nothing about real q_0. This is the Drinfeld–Kohno theorem [kohno1987, drinfeld1990, kassel1995], cited, not proved. For a real level the monodromy eigenvalues lie on the unit circle, so they cannot equal the real substrate value q_0 > 1 (proved). The real value is reached at the purely imaginary coupling \lambda_0=\ln q_0/(i\pi)\approx -0.0332\,i, and the theorem does hold there. Kohno's Remark 1.3.14 states that for any complex \lambda the correspondence of Theorem 1.2.8 holds when the R-matrix images \varphi(\gamma_k) of \gamma_k=(\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_{k-1})^k, 2\le k\le n, are diagonalizable, and that this holds when \varphi is completely reducible [kohno1987]. At real q_0>1, q_0 is not a root of unity, so V^{\otimes n}=\bigoplus_j V^{q}_j\otimes M^{q}_j is semisimple and \varphi(\gamma_k) acts on each isotypic block of V^{\otimes k} by a scalar (the ribbon twist), hence is diagonalizable. The intertwiner argument above uses only that q is not a root of unity, so it applies at \lambda_0 too. A numerical check at n=3 agrees: for pure braids \sigma_1^2,\sigma_2^2 and the products \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^2, \sigma_2^2\sigma_1^2, \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^{-2}, the KZ monodromy at \lambda_0 and the Jimbo R-matrix at q_0 have equal traces in every total-weight sector, up to the scalar q^{-1} per \sigma_i^2, to 10^{-15}, with the residual falling as h^4 under step refinement, and the opposite orientation q\mapsto q^{-1} fails by 0.70. So, with \mathrm{Hol} read as the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov holonomy at \lambda_0, the identity holds at the real pin, resting on the cited Kohno theorem and remark. Two pieces are proved: the two-strand case, where the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov transport is solved, shown unique, and its exchange operator equals q^{-1/2} times a weight-preserving conjugate of \check R(q), so that \mathrm{Tr}\big((K\otimes K)(P\,\mathrm{Hol})^k\big)=q^{-k/2}\,\mathrm{Tr}\big((K\otimes K)\check R^k\big) for all k; and the flatness of the n-point connection (KZ connection). A second, algebraic route to the \mathfrak{sl}_2 statement at every \lambda\notin\mathbb{Q} adapts Etingof–Motorin–Varchenko–Zhu. What stays open is different: whether the framework's own substrate connection is this Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection.

Explicit values

Evaluating at q_0 \approx 1.110 with Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) \approx 0.613 (\mathrm{SU}_q(2)/Temperley–Lieb) and h = q - q^{-1} \approx 0.209:

Particle Braid \beta_\mathcal{K} \int_A \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K}) Symbolic
\gamma (photon) \mathbf{1} 1 1
\sigma_0 (pol.) \sigma_0 z \approx 0.613 z
L_+ (gluon) \sigma_0\sigma_1 z^2 \approx 0.375 z^2
e^- (electron) \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \approx 0.691 hz^2 + z
4_1 (figure-eight) (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^2 \approx 0.280 \dfrac{q^8-q^6+q^4-q^2+1}{q^6+2q^4+q^2}

These constitute dimensionless ratios relative to the photon (\mathfrak{m}_{q,\gamma} = 1). Physical masses in MeV require a calibration constant E_0, determined by anchoring to one experimental value (e.g., the free neutron \beta-decay Q-value).
